answer: Keep the burette demonstration as a homework or next-lesson opener, but state plainly that draining water is only an approximate analogy for decay and that the teacher must trial it first. Add a concrete trial check (levels at equal intervals, about half every similar time) and a fallback to the dice evidence if the trial is not clean. This keeps the KICD activity without claiming a clean exponential result.

edits.old: (draining water is only an approximate analogy for decay; the teacher should trial it first)
edits.new: (draining water is only an approximate analogy for decay, because the flow rate falls with the water level and depends on the outlet. Before using it, the teacher trials it on the school's own burette: read the level every 30 seconds and check that the level falls by about half in roughly equal times. If it does not, learners use the dice-simulation curve as the half-life evidence and the burette is shown only as a timing exercise)
